rv.q: The more compelling is the sprawling “Midnight,” an intermittently gorgeous, often exasperating, utterly overstuffed quasi-opera at the Daryl Roth Theater, written by, directed by, choreographed by and starring Todrick Hall.
But though Hall’s dramatic ambition is large, his thematic ambition is slim: The musical lands on lessons that are naïvely pat, and then Hall closes the show with an odd lecture on numerology.
Midnight already sounds, looks, and innovates like the best new musical of the year.
Pairing extraordinary vocals with powerful storytelling, MIDNIGHT is an ambitious musical that challenges perspectives and leaves you with plenty to think about long after the final note.
But there's no denying someone else should have looked at all these elements, which might have made "Midnight" a more satisfying (and shorter) event.
Midnight is memorable for its thoughtful theme, unusually powerful vocal ensemble, its engaging (if repetitious) score, imaginative staging, and visual delights.
By the end you may find yourself in complete awe at the talent you’ve witnessed onstage and the genuine brilliance that Hall possesses in mind, body, and vocal cords.
But put together in context, these components create a strange, complex experience that’s not exactly unenjoyable, but somewhat dubious.

The trouble is that much of “Midnight” feels like just that, a showcase, both for Mr. Hall’s ideals and for the undeniably impressive gifts of his fellow actors, rather than a terribly compelling or even truly provocative story.
There are impactful and well-performed individual moments, but they are drowned in a sea of excess.
Todrick Hall’s Midnight wears its message in every lyric, and with voices this powerful carrying it, a few hours in someone else’s shoes is time well spent.
I cannot more strongly urge you to attend a performance of this show before its regrettably short engagement ends.
Todrick Hall’s Midnight is the bold, completely original theatrical adventure I have hungered for in Broadway’s recent years.
Currently playing at the Daryl Roth Theatre, it is, hands down, the best new musical I have seen this season.
Todrick has written all of himself
Between the moving story and the uplifting music and dancing, it is certainly well worth the time.
Todrick Hall was given the opportunity to create his own unique vision on stage, and to quote his fellow artistic traveler, he did not throw away his shot.
And in a world of safe Broadway retreads, something thought-provoking and surprising is to be commended.
With the right refinements, this production has the potential to take things to another level, giving Todrick and his incredibly talented cast the opportunity to rack up awards next season.
The result is a technically impressive production that moved me deeply before its central role reversal complicated my connection to the story.
Midnight has flashes of luminous greatness, but too often Hall does not know when to stop.
The score, the voices, the dancing, and the sheer imagination of the staging make this an extraordinary night of theater.
Driven by Hall’s endless ambition and a bevy of spectacular performances, Midnight strikes just when Broadway needs it the most.
From its powerful vocals to its elaborate costumes and ambitious storytelling, MIDNIGHT delivers a surprisingly grand theatrical experience.
So superb are the performers, however, I'd have happily stayed on for a third act hypothesizing yet another twist.
There are moments of musical theatre brilliance here.

cn.t: Hall's ambitious sung-through musical dazzles with extraordinary vocals and bold choreography, but critics find the nearly three-hour production overstuffed and unfocused, struggling to balance its provocative premise with execution.

vr.q: The entire show is amazing and beautiful and about humanity.
this is so freaking special I cannot stress this enough if you get a chance to come to the Daryl Roth go go
Extraordinary vocals, a sticky score, and a palpable energy make this new musical by Todrick Hall a must-see
Walked out of midnight feeling like I had seen something that was truly unique and wildly ambitious and completely original.
It feels like four shows in one.
Midnight is a show that has a lot to enjoy, but it is also far from a perfect musical.
